newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: UK's Compass buys stake in S.Africa's KKS.
newsitem.headline: UK's Compass buys stake in S.Africa's KKS.

text.p: South Africa's leading contractual catering company Kagiso Khulani Supervision Food Services (KKS) said on Wednesday it had sold a strategic equity stake to Britain's Compass Group Plc in a 133.4 million rand deal.
KKS said in a statement that the Tongaat-Hulett Group, which previously owned KKS, and FirstCorp Capital Investors have each sold their respective stakes.

"When 80 percent of (KKS) was acquired from the Tongaat-Hulett Group, and FirstCorp came on board, there was always the understanding that Tongaat-Hulett and FirstCorp would not be long term partners and would be disinvesting," said Eric Molobi, KKS chairman said.
Compass, which Molobi said had been seeking a South African partner, saw the deal as a opening into Africa.

"South Africa has been identified as a lucrative growth market and the partnership will privide Compass Group with a springboard into other African markets," said John Greenwood, managing director of Compass's U.K contract foodservice business.
The two groups will pioneer food courts in South Africa. This concept, developed by Compass, sees canteens transformed into facilities providing well-known fast food brands.
KKS, which is South Africa's first black-controlled catering company and employs 5,200 people, has forecast turnover for this year at 567 million rand.
Compass, with over 125,000 staff in over 40 countries and turnover of 3.3 billion stg last year, will introduce KKS to the latest technology, service and products.
